symbols.name: \(\theta,\vartheta\)
symbols.def: \(\theta(\widetilde P_n)=\widetilde P_n\{Y(0)=0\mid A=1,Y(1)=1\}\) and \(\vartheta(\widetilde P_n)=\widetilde P_n\{Y(1)=1\mid A=0,Y(0)=0\}\).

symbols.name: \(K,I_{k,n}\)
symbols.def: \(K\) is fixed and the deterministic balanced sets \(I_{k,n}\) are validation folds.

symbols.name: \(w,\Delta_n,\beta,\gamma,u,\xi\)
symbols.space: a simplex and compact Euclidean boxes

symbols.name: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha},\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PS}}_{n,\alpha},D_n\)
symbols.def: The LR sets are defined in \(\texttt{def:finite-lr}\) and \(\texttt{def:ps-inversion}\); \(D_n\) is a generic procedure.

symbols.name: \(\Lambda_j^{(3)}\)
symbols.def: \(\Lambda_j^{(3)}(t)\) is the conditional three-count likelihood-ratio statistic defined in \(\texttt{def:no-covariate-exhibit}\).

symbols.name: \(c_\psi\)
symbols.def: \(c_\psi\) is the rare-scale score-variance lower bound.

novel.justification: Protocol-fixed clinical case strata and pre-specified extreme-event thresholds can make the treated factual-event probability decrease with the row index.
Within the attainable Gaussian regime it excludes deterministic attribution; the local least-favorable pair has this property away from the endpoint \(t=1\).

definitions.name: Hölder ball
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)=\{g:[0,1]^p\to\mathbb R: \max_{|s|\le\lfloor\beta\rfloor}\lVert D^s g\rVert_\infty+\max_{|s|=\lfloor\beta\rfloor}\sup_{x\ne x'}|D^s g(x)-D^s g(x')|/\lVert x-x'\rVert^{\beta-\lfloor\beta\rfloor}\le L\}\).

definitions.name: clipped tensor-product B-spline sieve ERM
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\{e,0\}\), take degree \(r_j\ge\lceil\beta_j\rceil\), \(K_{j,n}\asymp(n/\log n)^{1/(2\beta_j+p)}\) equally spaced interior knots per coordinate, and \(J_{j,n}=(K_{j,n}+r_j+1)^p\). On each training complement, minimize Bernoulli logistic loss \(\sum_{i\notin I_{k,n}}[-A_i\log e_\beta(X_i)-(1-A_i)\log\{1-e_\beta(X_i)\}]\) over the deterministic compact propensity box, and minimize control-weighted squared loss \(\sum_{i\notin I_{k,n}}(1-A_i)\{Y_i-B_{0,n}(X_i)^\top\gamma\}^2\) over the deterministic compact control box. The boxes contain Hölder approximants; clip fitted functions to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) and \([0,1]\), respectively.

definitions.name: structural full-data class
definitions.construction: \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n=\{\widetilde P_n: \widetilde P_n\text{ satisfies \texttt{ass:consistency}, \texttt{ass:ignorability}, and \texttt{ass:monotonicity, and its observed projection satisfies \texttt{ass:overlap}, \texttt{ass:rare-event}, \texttt{ass:covariate-design}, \texttt{ass:holder-propensity}, and \texttt{ass:holder-control}}\}\).

definitions.name: attainable Gaussian sub-class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{LAN}}=\{P_n\in\mathcal M_n: \texttt{ass:score-nondegeneracy holds and }d_n\gg\max\{(\log n/n)^{2s_0},n(\log n/n)^{2(s_e+s_0)}\}\}\).

definitions.name: Borel finite empirical-support likelihood-ratio inversion
definitions.construction: Given \(Z_n\), set \(e_\beta(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]}\{B_{e,n}(x)^\top\beta\}\) and \(m_{0,\gamma}(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}\{B_{0,n}(x)^\top\gamma\}\). At labelled support points require \(w\in\Delta_n\), \(u_i\in[0,1]\), \(u_i=u_j\) when \(X_i=X_j\), \(m_{0,\gamma}(X_i)\le u_i\), and \(d(\xi)=\sum_iw_i e_\beta(X_i)u_i\in[0,\bar d]\). Put \(q_{i,11}=e_\beta(X_i)u_i\), \(q_{i,10}=e_\beta(X_i)(1-u_i)\), \(q_{i,01}=(1-e_\beta(X_i))m_{0,\gamma}(X_i)\), and \(q_{i,00}=(1-e_\beta(X_i))(1-m_{0,\gamma}(X_i))\). Let \(\Xi_n\) be this compact domain with the coefficient boxes and \(\Xi_n(t)=\{\xi\in\Xi_n:\sum_iw_ie_\beta(X_i)[(1-t)u_i-m_{0,\gamma}(X_i)]=0\}\). Let \(\Omega_{Z_n}=(\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{00,01,10,11\})^n\). For \(S=((L_j,C_j))_{j=1}^n\in\Omega_{Z_n}\), set \(P_\xi(S)=\prod_jw_{L_j}q_{L_j,C_j}\), \(\ell_\xi(S)=\sum_j[\log w_{L_j}+\log q_{L_j,C_j}]\), and \(\Lambda_n^*(t;S)=2[\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n}\ell_\xi(S)-\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}\ell_\xi(S)]\), with \(\log0=-\infty\) and \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\). Set \(S_{\mathrm{obs}}=((i,(A_i,Y_i)))_{i=1}^n\) and \(\Lambda_n(t)=\Lambda_n^*(t;S_{\mathrm{obs}})\). A simulated \((L_j,C_j)\) carries the newly simulated score mark \(\psi_{t,n}((X_{L_j},C_j);\widehat\eta_{-k(L_j),n})\); raw cells determine likelihood and marks are retained for score and LAN expansion. For every threshold choose \(\xi^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t,s}=\operatorname{lexmin}\arg\max_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}P_\xi\{\Lambda_n^*(t)\ge s\}\). Finite support, compactness, the measurable maximum theorem, and the fixed tie-break make the selector Borel. With independent \(U_n\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\), define \(p_n(t;S_{\mathrm{obs}},U_n)=\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}[P_\xi\{\Lambda_n^*(t)>\Lambda_n(t)\}+U_nP_\xi\{\Lambda_n^*(t)=\Lambda_n(t)\}]\), and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha}=\{t:p_n(t)>\alpha\}\), taking \([0,1]\) when \(N_{11,n}=0\).

definitions.name: treatment-and-outcome-swapped PS inversion
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PS}}_{n,\alpha}\) is \(\texttt{def:finite-lr}\) applied to \(\mathfrak T(X,A,Y)=(X,1-A,1-Y)\), with target \(\vartheta(\widetilde P_n)\) and factual probability \(d_n^{\mathrm{PS}}\).

definitions.name: bounded monotone least-favorable submodel
definitions.construction: For \(t\in[1/4,3/4]\), let \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^p)\), \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently, and conditional monotone types satisfy \(P\\{(Y(0),Y(1))=(1,1)\mid X\\}=2(1-t)d_n\), \(P\\{(Y(0),Y(1))=(0,1)\mid X\\}=2td_n\), and \(P\\{(Y(0),Y(1))=(0,0)\mid X\\}=1-2d_n\). Let \(P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\) be the observed marginal.

definitions.name: no-covariate likelihood-ratio exhibit
definitions.construction: In \(\texttt{def:least-favorable}\), \((p_{11},p_{01},p_{10},p_{00})=(d_n,(1-t)d_n,1/2-d_n,1/2-(1-t)d_n)\), and \(L(t,d_n)\propto d_n^{N_{11,n}}\{(1-t)d_n\}^{N_{01,n}}(1/2-d_n)^{N_{10,n}}\{1/2-(1-t)d_n\}^{N_{00,n}}\). Conditional on \(M_n=N_{11,n}+N_{01,n}\), \(N_{01,n}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(M_n,q_t)\) with \(q_t=(1-t)/(2-t)\). At \((N_{11,n},N_{01,n},N_{10,n},N_{00,n})=(2,1,8,9)\), \(M_n=3\), \(\widehat q=1/3\), \(\widehat t=1/2\), and \(\Lambda_n(t)=2[\log\{(1/3)/q_t\}+2\log\{(2/3)/(1-q_t)\}]\). For \(j=0,1,2,3\), set \(\Lambda_j^{(3)}(t)=2[j\log\{(j/3)/q_t\}+(3-j)\log\{((3-j)/3)/(1-q_t)\}]\), with \(0\log0=0\). The randomized upper-tail rule accepts exactly the values \(t\in[0,1]\) satisfying \(\sum_{j=0}^3{3\choose j}q_t^j(1-q_t)^{3-j}1\{\Lambda_j^{(3)}(t)>\Lambda_1^{(3)}(t)\}+U_n\sum_{j=0}^3{3\choose j}q_t^j(1-q_t)^{3-j}1\{\Lambda_j^{(3)}(t)=\Lambda_1^{(3)}(t)\}>\alpha\). If \(N_{11,n}=0\), inversion is \([0,1]\); for \(0<d_n<1/2\) and \(0<t<1\), every displayed likelihood denominator is nonzero.

definitions.name: selected-event inference handle
definitions.construction: For a threshold or projection-index class fixed before outcome analysis, form the joint family of \(\texttt{def:finite-lr}\) experiments, calibrate a supremum likelihood ratio over the class before selecting an index, and invert at the selected index.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), independently draw the row from the observed projection of an admitted full-data law.
sampling_model.units: Each unit supplies \(X\), binary \(A\), and binary \(Y\).
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency, ignorability, monotonicity, and overlap identify PN and PS.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold clipped tensor-product B-spline ERM fits propensity by logistic loss and \(m_0\) only on control training observations.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:ignorability}\), \(\texttt{ass:monotonicity}\), and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), \(\theta(\widetilde P_n)=\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n)\) and \(\vartheta(\widetilde P_n)=\Theta_{\mathrm{PS}}(P_n)\). Thus any two admitted full-data extensions with the same observed marginal have the same PN and PS values, and \(E_{P_n}[\psi_{\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n),n}(O;\eta_n)]=0\).
statements.justification: It turns the causal targets into extension-invariant observed-law functionals and supplies the marginal null.
statements.gap: Tian and Wu (2025) identify regular PN and PS, but do not formulate the finite-support marginal-null experiment.
statements.consumer: It licenses the PN and PS likelihood-ratio targets.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{ass:iid-row}\), \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), \(\texttt{ass:covariate-design}\), \(\texttt{ass:holder-propensity}\), and \(\texttt{ass:holder-control}\), \(\texttt{def:crossfit}\) satisfies \(\max_{k\le K}(\lVert\widehat e_{-k,n}-e_n\rVert_{2,P_n}\vee\lVert\widehat e_{-k,n}-e_n\rVert_\infty)=O_{P_n}(a_{e,n})\) and \(\max_{k\le K}\lVert\widehat m_{0,-k,n}-m_{0,n}\rVert_{2,P_n}=O_{P_n}(a_{0,n})\). With \(\delta_e=\widehat e-e\) and \(\delta_0=\widehat m_0-m_0\), \(E[\psi_t(O;\widehat\eta)-\psi_t(O;\eta)\mid\widehat\eta]=E[\delta_e(X)\delta_0(X)/(1-\widehat e(X))]\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\psi_t(O;\widehat\eta)-\psi_t(O;\eta)\mid\widehat\eta)\lesssim a_{0,n}^2+d_na_{e,n}^2\). Consequently the cross-fit difference is \(O_{P_n}(a_{0,n}/\sqrt n+\sqrt{d_n/n}a_{e,n}+a_{e,n}a_{0,n})\), uniformly in \(t\), and is \(o_{P_n}(\sqrt{d_n/n})\) on \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{LAN}}\).
statements.justification: It derives the nuisance remainder from primitive Hölder laws instead of imposing estimator-dependent class membership.
statements.gap: Regular DML conditions do not expose the \(d_n\)-scaled product bias and control-regression noise.
statements.consumer: It supplies the only admissible Gaussian-regime remainder for likelihood transfer.

statements.statement: If \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), \(\varepsilon\le1/2\le1-\varepsilon\), \(2\bar d\le1\), and the Hölder radii contain the constants \(e_n\equiv1/2\) and \(m_{0,n}\equiv2(1-t)d_n\), then \(P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\in\mathcal M_n\), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t})=t\), and its factual probability is \(d_n\). The local pair \(t=1/2\pm h\min\{1,(nd_n)^{-1/2}\}\) also satisfies score nondegeneracy.
statements.justification: It certifies the causal and Hölder membership of the lower-bound pair without claiming any estimator-dependent property.
statements.gap: Generic ratio lower bounds do not verify monotonicity, overlap, and Hölder membership together.
statements.consumer: It transfers the testing lower bound to the structural causal class.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), randomized inversion in \(\texttt{def:finite-lr}\) has exact uniform \(1-\alpha\) coverage over its finite empirical-support experiment at every count. If \(nd_n=O(1)\), its diameter is at most one, its limit is the corresponding marked-Poisson likelihood-ratio experiment, and the zero factual-count rule is \([0,1]\). The treatment-and-outcome-swapped construction has the same properties for PS. This exact assertion is only for the finite profiling experiment.
statements.justification: Discrete least-favorable randomization supplies honest finite-information calibration without a Gaussian approximation.
statements.gap: Huwang (1995) shows nonuniform normal-binomial coverage; McGrath and Burke (2024) compare rare-binomial coverage and relative margins, neither treats learned causal score cells.
statements.consumer: It provides valid rare-count calibration for fixed-support attribution analyses.

statements.statement: For every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{LAN}}\), the finite/sieve likelihood transfers to the observed Hölder law, \(\texttt{def:finite-lr}\) has conditional LAN at scale \(\sqrt{nd_n}\), its influence function is \(d_n^{-1}\psi_{\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n),n}(O;\eta_n)\), equal to the Tian--Wu monotone-PN efficient influence function, and its expected diameter is \(O((nd_n)^{-1/2})\). For \(d_n=n^{-b}\), ignoring displayed logarithmic boundaries, this regime is \(0\le b<\min\{1,2s_0,2(s_e+s_0)-1\}\); it is nonempty only if \(s_e+s_0>1/2\). The swapped conclusion holds for PS.
statements.justification: It gives the attainable continuous-law Gaussian endpoint at the primitive smoothness–rarity frontier.
statements.gap: Tian and Wu (2025) prove the regular fixed-law PN/PS limit, not this \(d_n\)-indexed transfer region.
statements.consumer: It yields efficient rare-event PN/PS intervals whenever effective information dominates spline learning error.

statements.statement: Conjecture 1 (not yet proved): for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), transfer of \(\texttt{def:finite-lr}\) to the whole structural class satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n}P_n\{\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n)\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n}E_{P_n}[\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha})]/\min\{1,[nd_n]^{-1/2}\}\le C_\alpha\), with identical PS assertions. When \(nd_n\to\lambda<\infty\), the marked-Poisson boundary has nonshrinking expected diameter; when \(nd_n\to\infty\), the claim includes the required all-sequence likelihood transfer and LAN. Outside the bounded-count result and \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{LAN}}\), this remains open because first-order fixed-smoothness learning need not make the rare-scale remainder negligible.
statements.justification: This is the unresolved adaptive bridge between exact marked-Poisson inversion and the attainable Gaussian theorem.
statements.gap: It would strictly tighten Tian and Wu's regular-only inference by adding an honest rare-count and Poisson regime. Mikusheva and Sun (2022) obtain uniformly valid inversion for many weak instruments through a jackknifed Anderson--Rubin statistic; their linear-IV weak-identification experiment has neither a bounded PN ratio, learned outcome nuisances, nor a Poisson factual-count boundary.
statements.consumer: It would deliver one confidence-set construction across rare climate and stroke-attribution regimes.

statements.statement: For every measurable \(D_n\) with \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n}P_n\{\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n)\in D_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n}E_{P_n}[\operatorname{diam}(D_n)]/\min\{1,[nd_n]^{-1/2}\}\ge c_\alpha\). In the certified local pair from \(\texttt{lem:lf-membership}\), product Kullback--Leibler divergence is at most \(16h^2\); the swap gives PS. Hence \(nd_n\to\lambda<\infty\) forces nonshrinking expected diameter for every uniformly honest procedure.
statements.justification: It is the causal effective-count converse matching the claimed frontier order.
statements.gap: Gleser and Hwang (1987) provide a ratio-impossibility template, not this bounded monotone-PN submodel.
statements.consumer: It distinguishes unavoidable finite information from defects of a particular interval.

statements.statement: Can \(\texttt{def:selection-handle}\) retain the coverage and diameter conclusions of Conjecture 1 after a climate threshold or multivariate projection is selected to maximize causal evidence?
statements.justification: Selection changes both the causal target and the effective factual count.
statements.gap: Hannart and Naveau (2018) and Kiriliouk and Naveau (2020) optimize climate causal evidence without selection-honest learned-score inversion.
statements.consumer: It would support valid uncertainty statements for selected climate events.

tldr: The proposal studies point-identified PN and PS when their factual conditioning event is rare. A randomized empirical-support likelihood-ratio inversion retains the four observed treatment-outcome cells, empirical covariate weights, and score marks; it is exactly calibrated in its finite experiment and has a marked-Poisson boundary. Primitive design, overlap, monotonicity, and Hölder conditions imply the spline-learning remainder and identify the attainable Gaussian region. A certified monotone causal submodel gives the matching expected-diameter lower bound. The extension of the construction to the full continuous-law frontier outside that Gaussian region remains Conjecture 1.

project_justification.gap: Regular PN and PS inference does not cover a vanishing factual conditioning probability, and generic rare-binomial intervals do not accommodate causal nuisance learning.
project_justification.niche: Empirical-likelihood weights retain the random-covariate component of the marginal PN null, while randomized calibration handles a finite score-cell experiment.
project_justification.fill: The project gives exact finite-experiment rare-count inference, an attainable smoothness–rarity Gaussian theorem, a certified causal lower bound, and a sharply stated all-regime conjecture.

related_work: Tian and Wu (2025), \(\textit{Semiparametric efficient inference for the probability of necessary and sufficient causation}\), Statistics in Medicine, doi: \(10.1002/\mathrm{sim}.70242\), is the regular-law comparator: it derives monotonicity-based efficient influence functions and regular semiparametric inference for PN and PS; it does not address triangular rare-event sequences, finite-count randomized inversion, marked-Poisson limits, or honest diameter frontiers. Cai and Kuroki (2005) provide direct regular variance estimators for three probabilities of causation. Cuellar and Kennedy (2020) study a regular projection of probability of causation, while Zhang, Wang, and Miao (2025) study partially identified PN bounds. Chernozhukov et al. (2018) supply cross-fitting architecture and Chen (2007) supplies spline rates. Mikusheva and Sun (2022) establish uniformly sized jackknifed Anderson--Rubin inversion under many weak instruments; its linear-IV experiment motivates inversion but does not contain a rare factual PN event, a bounded PN ratio, or learned outcome regression. Huwang (1995) supplies the nonuniform normal-approximation failure claim; McGrath and Burke (2024) motivate rare-binomial coverage and relative-margin comparisons. Gleser and Hwang (1987) motivate the expected-diameter converse. Hannart and Naveau (2018) supply the rare climate PN consumer.
honest_scope: The finite-experiment theorem is exact only for its empirical-support profiling law. Over continuous Hölder laws, Gaussian recovery and shrinking diameter are claimed only on \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{LAN}}\); fixed first-order smoothness permits diverging effective counts outside that region. At fixed positive \(d_n\), the Gaussian result reduces to the Tian--Wu regular efficient benchmark. Conjecture 1 is the remaining all-regime transfer problem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sections 2--3 identify monotone PN and PS, derive efficient influence functions, and establish regular large-sample inference.
Regular variance-inference context for probabilities of causation.
A nonparametric influence-function estimator gives regular inference for a projection of probability of causation.
Inference is developed for generally partially identified PN bounds.
A familiar normal-approximation binomial interval lacks uniform asymptotic coverage.
Ratio-like zero-information models can preclude finite expected-diameter confidence sets.
A jackknifed Anderson--Rubin test gives uniformly valid inference in linear IV models with many weak instruments.
